correctness.rationale: The analytic factorization exactly reduces three unknowns to a single second divided difference. For t>0 the second derivative of sqrt(u)tanh(t sqrt(u)) is strictly negative because tanh(x)-x sech(x)^2 has positive derivative, giving F′(t)<0. Its range is all negative reals, hence inversion and admissibility are exact. Two readings leave a physical continuum. A Taylor expansion and two-data-preserving path prove universal quartic order and sharp inverse exponent 1/4. Seven-file package includes a finite reproducibility code, not mistaken for an all-parameter proof.
